drug_class: CGRP antagonist (calcitonin gene-related peptide monoclonal antibody)
purpose: Ajovy is used to prevent migraines in adults. It helps reduce how often you get migraines and can make them less severe when they do happen. It is not used to treat a migraine once it has already started.
how_it_works: Migraines are linked to a protein in your body called CGRP, which plays a big role in causing migraine pain. Ajovy is a special antibody that blocks this protein from doing its job. By blocking CGRP, it helps stop migraines before they even begin.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is redness, pain, itching, or a small bump at the injection site where you give yourself the shot. Some people may also notice mild bruising or swelling at that spot.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to fremanezumab or any of its ingredients, as serious allergic reactions can happen. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before starting this medication. If you notice signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing, seek medical help right away.
typical_dosing: Ajovy is given as an injection under the skin. You can take it one of two ways: either one injection of 225 mg once a month, or three injections of 225 mg each (totaling 675 mg) once every three months. Your doctor will help you decide which schedule works best for you.
